The book states the representations V(O,U) are 'pairwise nonisomorphic,' meaning distinct (orbit, irrep) pairs yield non-isomorphic representations. The Lean statement only asserts that V(χ₁,U₁) ≅ V(χ₂,U₂) implies χ₁ and χ₂ are in the same G-orbit (∃ g, dualSmul g χ₁ = χ₂). It drops the second half: that the stabilizer representations U₁ and U₂ (conjugated to a common stabilizer) must be isomorphic. A pair with the same orbit but non-isomorphic U-components would still be incorrectly allowed by the Lean statement. Parts (i), (iii), (iv) match the book faithfully.
